articles.title: Phoenix
articles.summary: Rows of small gold-orange flame tips on near-black, like a repeating feathery flame pattern. Reads as a dark brown-black with a fine golden-orange dot grid, like a lit candle field or a glowing pegboard; warm and quiet, with an ember shimmer.
articles.what: Gold/orange feathery phoenix flames Up close: Orderly staggered rows of tiny upright glowing ticks about 10px tall and 25px apart, each pale gold at the core fading to orange-red, on a near-black maroon ground with a faint red glow around each. Rows ripple slightly. It looks more like a grid of candle flames or embers than long feathery flame. From a distance: Reads as a dark brown-black with a fine golden-orange dot grid, like a lit candle field or a glowing pegboard; warm and quiet, with an ember shimmer. Measured spec (average): metal 139, roughness 113, coat 124. Shine: satin. Metal: medium. It brings its own colours.
when: Fits: stock car, dirt late model, show car.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Phoenix" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Hood, doors, roof and quarter panels: the rows read on big flats
Whole body also works: the tone stays dark
White or yellow block numbers with a thick black outline read; gold or orange numbers vanish into the dots.
Large flame or tribal graphics in orange or gold: the base supplies the glow, the graphic supplies the shape
Pairs well with: black, red, chrome, cream.
pitfalls: Not a flame graphic: flames are tiny repeated ticks, with no licks or tongues
Not gold flake: the glints are a regular grid of vertical ticks, not random flecks
Avoid: dark base hides flames at night, small flames read as noise far away.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 139 (strong pearl or anodized metal), roughness 113 (satin or eggshell), clearcoat 124 (satin or weak clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal and clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.

Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour.
